newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee widens fall in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee widens fall in slow trade.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures extended their fall on Monday in sympathy with New York but trading was slow and dominated by jobbers.
Traders said the day's volume at 2,415 lots made up of 500 actual trades and about 1,000 by jobbers. There was just 500 lots of outrights.
Market participants were said to have turned to the more active cocoa futures which saw heavy spec long liquidation.
September, the benchmark contract, gave up its slight gains to end the day $58 down at $1,547 per tonne -- the session's low.
Other positions also posted double-digit losses.
Like in New York, market sentiment could be weighed down by the no-frost forecast for Brazil through the end of July, traditionally the end to the frost season in the key producing nation.
"But things are quiet and much of the frost premium is already out of the market," broker GNI said.
Chart-wise, traders said the market's technical outlook could improve slightly if September holds above $1,600 after it had rebounded from last week's low of $1,530.
New York-traded arabica coffee futures headed lower from the start on sell-stops, pushing the September contract to a low at 156 cents a lb. By 1642 GMT, it stood 6.05 cents lower at 158.25.

On the fundamental front, traders in London played down concerns voiced by some quarters in the U.S. trade over the weekend that a hurricane could potentially damange coffee stored in New Orleans warehouses or disrupt coffee shipments to New Orleans.
"There is a hurricane in New Orleans and some people were afraid it could hit warehouses," one U.S. trader said one Friday.
But traders in London said only heavy rains were forecast in that area.
Monday is the last day for trading of July contract on the New York futures.
The U.S. CFTC Commitment of Traders report on Friday showed the most balanced picture in a long while, GNI said. The commercial side is only marginally net short and the funds only marginally long.
